text.p: Dutch food group Nutricia said on Thursday its 1996 net profits surged 52.6 percent to 232 million guilders ($122.7 million) and forecast significantly higher earnings in 1997.
"Combined with expected market developments, the results in the current financial year will show a substantial rise, barring unforseen circumstances," the company said in a statement.
The company also said it would split its shares five for one and announced it was changing the name of the business to Numico in order to separate the firm's name from that of its brands.

The result was close to analysts' expectations, which had ranged between 220 and 237 million guilders. The announcement was made after Amsterdam bourse closing, when Nutricia shares had finished up 10.00 guilders at 290.00.
Turnover rose 51 percent to 2.91 billion guilders and operating profits soared 62.2 percent to 340 million guilders, the company said in a statement.

Analysts had expected the continuing integration of the Milupa baby food business acquired in 1995 to again prove the engine of growth and Nutricia said its German daughter had contributed roughly 83 million guilders to the operating profit.
The company said that, excluding the effect of the Milupa takeover, autonomous growth had reached 7.1 percent in 1996.

Nutricia's earnings per share increased by nearly 40 percent to 9.58 guilders per share and the dividend was increased to 3.20 guilders from 2.10. The share split will lower the nominal value per share from 2.50 to 0.50 guilders. -- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000, Fax +31 20 504 5040 ($ = 1.891 Dutch Guilders)
